prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Theia on an oblique collision course: The established smaller rough Theia approaches the larger Earth's edge along one strongly oblique path, a dark gap remains. Avoid: Before contact; no collision flash, finished disk or second Moon.
2. Earth and debris after a giant impact: One surviving orange cracked Earth and a broad asymmetric plume of hot silicate debris flung from its limb. Avoid: Planet unmistakably survives; no total star-like explosion or formed Moon.
3. The surviving, remelted Earth: The same Earth after impact, broadly remelted orange with two broken basalt patches and a short residual debris arc. Avoid: Keep Earth identity; changed surface, not a newly created second planet.
4. Orbiting Moon-forming debris: A broad tilted broken disk of hot rocky debris surrounds the same remelted Earth, no separate satellite. Avoid: Earth at centre instead of Sun; no Moon before accumulation.
5. Debris escaping the Earth–Moon system: Several hot fragments peel away from a cropped Earth's limb on open outward-diverging paths. Avoid: Paths leave the field; no closed orbit and no inward trajectories.
6. Beyond the tidal disruption region: Near Earth a small rubble clump separates; farther away a compact clump persists, divided only by space. Avoid: Differential tidal effect schematic; no solid boundary fence or numerical threshold ring.
7. Collisions among orbiting debris: Two orbiting rough fragments meet within a short curved debris arc and leave different small paths. Avoid: Shared Earth-orbit context; angular-momentum exchange without a planet-scale flash.
8. A spreading ring of rock: The same Earth-centred debris disk widens, with sparse inner fragments turning inward and outer fragments spreading away. Avoid: One loose evolving disk, not a rigid ring; no formed Moon.
9. Growing moonlets: Three unequal rough glowing clumps gather beyond a cropped Earth's distant limb, few small fragments between. Avoid: Multiple lunar precursors, no full pale Moon or closed solid orbital track.
10. A hot young Moon: One round smaller satellite with amber molten surface and thin dark cooling streaks, simple even limb. Avoid: Lunar family stays smaller and smoother than Earth; no familiar maria.
11. Rock falling back toward Earth: A short arc of fragments curves downward into the same molten Earth's upper limb, one small impact glow. Avoid: Clearly returning toward Earth, not escaping or forming the Moon.
12. Earth remade by falling debris: The same remelted Earth has a fresh localized amber impact scar and sparse returning debris fading nearby. Avoid: Keep existing dark basalt regions in plausible altered form; no new water sea.
13. Crystals in the lunar magma ocean: A lunar magma section shows separate pale ivory platy crystals forming in amber melt. Avoid: Pale lunar crystal family, still separate within melt rather than complete crust.
14. A floating feldspar-rich layer: The same pale plates collect into a thin uneven layer at the top of a lunar amber melt section. Avoid: Buoyant accumulation at surface, not imported rocks or a full Moon globe.
15. The Moon with a pale early crust: A pale gray-ivory Moon with subtle rough highland-like grain and a few small irregular relief marks. Avoid: No familiar dark maria, glowing heat halo, face or modern lunar map.
16. Volatiles dissolved in Earth’s melt: A broad amber melt section beneath dark crust, smooth liquid with subtle diffuse internal texture and no separate bubbles. Avoid: Dissolved gases are invisible; never blue water pockets or gas beads before exsolution.
